focus_areas: Document open, flags and page analysis (src/peditor/worker/analyzer.py)

findings.title: Non-frozen worker launched with `python -m peditor.worker` puts cwd first on sys.path
findings.description: worker_command() returns [sys.executable, '-m', 'peditor.worker']; _WorkerProcess.__init__ (service.py:52-59) starts it with no cwd= and no -I/-P. With -m, Python prepends the current directory to sys.path, so peditor/ or pymupdf.py/pikepdf.py in the operator's cwd are imported by the worker before site-packages. The CLI entry (console script) has no cwd entry, so only the worker is exposed.
findings.exploit_scenario: Victim extracts an attacker ZIP containing case.pdf plus pymupdf.py, cd's into it and runs `peditor analyze case.pdf --out out`; the worker imports the planted module and executes code as the user.
findings.recommendation: Launch the worker with `-I` (or `-P`/PYTHONSAFEPATH=1) and an explicit safe cwd.

findings.title: Per-request timeout resets on every line; a compromised worker can hang the main process indefinitely
findings.description: _exchange loops on worker.lines.get(timeout=self.timeout); the timeout is per line. Lines whose request_id is neither the current id nor None hit `continue` with no deadline, while _call holds self._lock, blocking all other calls. The reader thread fills an unbounded queue.
findings.exploit_scenario: Worker compromised via a MuPDF/qpdf bug emits {"request_id":"x",...} every second; UI/CLI freezes forever, timeout/restart never fires.
findings.recommendation: Use one absolute deadline per request; treat mismatched request_id as a protocol violation (restart + WORKER_FAILED); bound the queue.

findings.title: Owner-password-only encrypted PDF (empty user password) is not flagged and is classified support
findings.description: Encryption is detected only via mu.needs_pass and pikepdf.PasswordError. A PDF with an empty user password and owner restrictions opens in both without a password, so flags['encrypted'] stays False and status is support; mu.is_encrypted / pike.is_encrypted are never checked.
findings.exploit_scenario: A 'no modification' restricted PDF is marked editable; a later pikepdf save() drops encryption and permission restrictions.
findings.recommendation: Also reject when mu.is_encrypted or pike.is_encrypted (or /Encrypt in trailer).

findings.title: Signature detection ignores inherited /FT, fields deeper than 32 levels, and widgets not in /AcroForm/Fields
findings.description: _is_signed requires /FT /Sig and /V on the same dict; /FT is inheritable. _fields stops at depth > 32 silently. Only /AcroForm/Fields and /Perms are scanned, not page /Annots widgets.
findings.exploit_scenario: A signed PDF whose /FT /Sig sits on a parent field is classified editable; editing invalidates the signature without SIGNED_DOCUMENT rejection.
findings.recommendation: Resolve inherited /FT; treat any /V with /Type /Sig or /ByteRange as signed; scan page widgets; treat depth overflow as reject.

findings.title: Active-content scan misses outlines, AcroForm field /AA, many action types and annotation kinds
findings.description: _active_content checks Root /OpenAction, Root/page /AA, /Names JavaScript/EmbeddedFiles keys, page annotation /A,/AA and FileAttachment. It does not walk /Outlines actions, field-level /AA on non-widget fields, action types other than JavaScript/Launch (SubmitForm, ImportData, GoToR, GoToE, Rendition, RichMediaExecute), RichMedia/Screen/Movie/Sound annotations, or action arrays.
findings.exploit_scenario: JavaScript placed in a bookmark action or in a field /AA /K keystroke action yields a 'support' classification.
findings.recommendation: Walk outlines and all fields/annotations with cycle detection; use an allowlist of permitted action types; handle action arrays.

findings.title: Form XObject fan-out is unbounded: N^8 work and memory
findings.description: _do caps depth (MAX_FORM_DEPTH=8) and direct cycles, but a Form may Do the same child any number of times; each visit re-parses the stream (no cache) and appends runs/images to self.result.
findings.exploit_scenario: 8-level chain where each level contains ~100 '/Next Do'; a few KB file triggers ~100^8 executions, gigabytes of RAM before the 30 s timeout.
findings.recommendation: Add a per-interpret budget (operators, Form invocations, runs/images) and cache parsed instructions per objgen.

findings.title: CIDFont /W range form expands an attacker-chosen range into a dict with no bound
findings.description: _cid_widths: for `c_first c_last w`, `for cid in range(first, last + 1): widths[cid] = value` with no cap; reached on any Tf using the font.
findings.exploit_scenario: /W [0 4000000000 500] in a few-hundred-byte PDF makes the worker allocate tens of GB before the timeout.
findings.recommendation: Clamp CIDs to 0..65535 and cap entries, or store ranges lazily.

findings.title: ToUnicode bfrange expansion unbounded per range and in total
findings.description: parse_cmap: lo/hi hex has no length limit; each range expands up to ~1.1M entries before chr() overflows; thousands of ranges in a small compressed stream build billions of entries. No decompressed-size cap.
findings.exploit_scenario: 5,000 bfrange lines of ~1M entries each in a few-KB Flate stream exhaust memory.
findings.recommendation: Reject ranges with hi-lo > 255 or source > 4 hex digits; cap total entries and the ToUnicode stream size.

findings.title: analyze() trusts worker result shape/content; unvalidated bytes written as .png; uncaught exceptions print tracebacks
findings.description: Only ServiceError is caught; malformed results raise KeyError/TypeError/binascii.Error; OSError messages include full output path; png_base64 not checked for PNG signature; NaN accepted into report.json.
findings.exploit_scenario: Compromised worker returns non-PNG bytes or malformed structures; CLI writes arbitrary bytes as page PNG or dumps a traceback.
findings.recommendation: Validate results (page_index range, PNG signature, strict base64), catch Exception/OSError with fixed codes, allow_nan=False.

findings.title: CLI prints worker-supplied error code without allow-list validation
findings.description: ServiceError.code comes from the worker response (service.py:245) unchecked; cli.py prints it verbatim to stderr; can carry document text, paths or terminal escape sequences.
findings.exploit_scenario: Compromised worker returns an error code containing ESC sequences or document text; printed to terminal/CI logs.
findings.recommendation: Map codes not in ERROR_CODES|PROTOCOL_ERROR_CODES to WORKER_FAILED; use fixed local messages.

findings.title: find_text collects unbounded overlapping matches over worker-supplied glyphs
findings.description: O(matches x len(wanted)) time/memory; glyph['c'] not type-checked so spans can misalign.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1M identical glyphs and a 1,000-char repeated search hang the UI process.
findings.recommendation: Cap matches, non-overlapping search, require str for c, bound glyph count.

findings.title: Main process keys documents by worker-chosen document_id; a compromised worker can overwrite another document's handle
findings.description: open_document stores self._docs[result['document_id']] without collision check; reopen-by-path then uses the wrong path; worker also supplies the sha256 used for the external-modification check.
findings.exploit_scenario: Malicious doc B returns doc A's id; A's handle now refers to B's path/content.
findings.recommendation: Generate handles in the main process (uuid4); reject duplicate/ill-formed worker ids.

findings.title: Unsynchronized _docs / worker_id state across _doc_call, _restart, _ensure_worker, open/close
findings.description: _doc_call reads/updates worker_id outside _lock; _restart/_ensure_worker iterate _docs while other threads mutate it; cancel() may kill a worker serving a later request.
findings.exploit_scenario: Concurrent UI open/close during a worker restart raises RuntimeError or sends stale ids.
findings.recommendation: Hold _lock across _doc_call and _docs mutations; iterate over a copy; check target request under lock in cancel().

findings.title: Worker responses not schema-checked: crafted shapes raise non-ServiceError exceptions and skip restart
findings.description: decode only checks dict; response['result'] KeyError, error.get AttributeError if error is not a dict; forged codes/messages pass through; worker not restarted on these paths.
findings.exploit_scenario: Compromised worker returns result [1] or error 'x'; main process raises TypeError/AttributeError, worker stays alive.
findings.recommendation: Validate per-operation schema; on violation restart and raise WORKER_FAILED; wrap unexpected exceptions.

findings.title: Exponential traversal in _fields with shared or self-referencing /Kids (depth-bounded only)
findings.description: _fields has no visited set; A /Kids [A A] yields ~2^33 items within the depth bound of 32.
findings.exploit_scenario: Small crafted PDF pins the worker CPU until the 30 s timeout on every open.
findings.recommendation: Track visited objgen; budget total nodes; treat cycles as MALFORMED_DOCUMENT.

findings.title: page_geometry ignores inherited /CropBox and /UserUnit; may diverge from MuPDF geometry
findings.description: Reads /CropBox only from the page dict; ignores /UserUnit; int(/Rotate) truncates; crop outside media yields inverted box.
findings.exploit_scenario: Inherited CropBox causes mismatched coordinate frames for UI overlay (mostly fail-safe via glyph location check).
findings.recommendation: Use inherited attribute resolution or MuPDF's cropbox/rotation; reject UserUnit != 1; validate Rotate and non-empty crop.

findings.title: render_page pixmap size bounded only by DPI, not by pixel area
findings.description: get_pixmap(dpi=dpi) with attacker-controlled page box/UserUnit; a 14400 pt page at 300 dpi requests ~10 GB.
findings.exploit_scenario: Huge MediaBox page rendered at default DPI drives worker memory to many GB.
findings.recommendation: Compute pixel count before rendering; reject or clamp above a cap (e.g. 50 MP).

findings.title: Unbounded q-stack depth with growing clip lists gives quadratic memory
findings.description: Each q copies gs (including the clip list); clips grow with each W n; no caps; ImageUse also copies clips.
findings.exploit_scenario: 200k 're W n' then 200k 'q' in a compressible stream allocates ~4e10 list slots.
findings.recommendation: Cap q depth and clips per state; keep an intersected bbox instead of a list.

findings.title: Huge operands produce inf/NaN matrices that bypass layout checks and cross IPC
findings.description: _num is plain float(); multiply yields inf/NaN without exception; NaN CTM passes the analyzer's layout checks (comparisons with NaN are False); json.dumps allows NaN.
findings.exploit_scenario: cm with 300-digit reals drives CTM to NaN; image reported as supported with NaN bboxes sent to the UI.
findings.recommendation: Reject non-finite/huge operands in _num; check finiteness after multiply; json.dumps(allow_nan=False).

findings.title: Non-dictionary /Resources raises AttributeError that escapes the per-operator handler and fails the whole request
findings.description: resources is only truthiness-checked; /Resources 5 makes resources.get raise AttributeError, not in the caught tuple; whole request returns WORKER_FAILED instead of a page-level MALFORMED_DOCUMENT.
findings.exploit_scenario: PDF with /Resources 1 makes analysis of the file fail.
findings.recommendation: Normalize resources to pikepdf.Dictionary; widen the handler.

findings.title: Malformed font dictionaries raise uncaught exception types; whole page fails
findings.description: DescendantFonts [/Foo] -> AttributeError; non-dict FontDescriptor -> AttributeError; escapes the Tf handler to server.py generic handler (WORKER_FAILED).
findings.exploit_scenario: One malformed font resource blocks analysis of all text on the page.
findings.recommendation: Type-check objects; mark font unsupported on any parse error.

findings.title: Quadratic regex scanning in parse_cmap on crafted ToUnicode text
findings.description: Lazy `beginbfchar(.*?)endbfchar` with N unmatched begins is O(N*len); `\[[^\]]*\]` alternative also quadratic on unclosed brackets; stream size uncapped.
findings.exploit_scenario: Few-MB ToUnicode of repeated 'beginbfrange <><>[' burns CPU until the timeout.
findings.recommendation: Cap stream length; linear tokenizer; bound array scans.

findings.title: Lone surrogate code points from /Differences or bfrange increments make inspect_page fail with UnicodeEncodeError
findings.description: _glyph_name_unicode accepts uniD800-uniDFFF; bfrange increments can step into surrogates; _target_id encodes utf-8 -> UnicodeEncodeError -> WORKER_FAILED; if reaching protocol.encode it could escape serve().
findings.exploit_scenario: /Differences [65 /uniD800] with (A) Tj makes the page permanently un-analyzable.
findings.recommendation: Reject surrogates and > 0x10FFFF; defensive encoding in _target_id; catch encode errors in serve().
